mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays near its current depressed level while TRANSIT remains below baseline, weekday foot traffic to shops will stay weak and RETAIL_REC will drift lower over the next four weeks. This is a direct commuting-to-shopping channel that should show up as no rebound in retail visits.
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not improve from current levels.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in RESIDENTIAL time signals substitution away from out-of-home activity; when people spend more time at home, discretionary retail visits fall within 1 to 2 weeks. The current elevated RESIDENTIAL series should therefore push RETAIL_REC downward soon after the snapshot.
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above its recent weekly average.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp upswing in PARKS mobility diverts discretionary time toward outdoor leisure instead of shopping trips, and retail mobility weakens over the next one to four weeks. The latest park drop must reverse first; without that rebound, retail will not recover.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses above its prior 2-week mean by at least 5 points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was -25.9 at t-1w and -15.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises even though PARKS stays at or above its pre-trigger level for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains deeply negative and WORKPLACES do not recover together, the city is still operating under movement frictions that suppress shopping trips. Under that regime, retail mobility should stay below the previous four-week mean over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -20 and WORKPLACES remains below -5 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises for four straight weeks while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both stay in the stated depressed range.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run bounce in GROCERY_PHARM captures essential trips and neighborhood activity that spills into adjacent convenience retail, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week. Because the current series is already above baseline, a further increase should translate quickly into higher retail mobility.
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM moves higher from the current week.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both rise together, the pattern indicates a substitution toward local, non-retail activities that crowds out discretionary shopping. The joint increase should suppress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks more strongly than either series alone.
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days while both PARKS and RESIDENTIAL are higher than their current weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES after a period of suppression marks reopening momentum that should feed retail demand with a lag. If both series improve from current levels, RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next four weeks than over the previous four.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -20 and WORKPLACES rises above -5
evidence_refs: fact:both series are still below baseline in the snapshot
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over 28 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES clear the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC move in opposite directions for one week, it signals substitution between essential and discretionary trips; if grocery visits keep rising while retail stays weak, retail mobility will be lower over the following month. This mechanism fails if grocery gains are driven by one-off stock-up behavior that does not persist.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM increases while RETAIL_REC remains below -5
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated and RETAIL_REC remains below the trigger level.
